title: Batch enqueue
task_summary: Add a bounded batch operation to the existing in-memory queue without breaking single-item callers.

required_outcomes.outcome: The queue provides one operation that accepts a group of items, with 100 as the default maximum batch size.
required_outcomes.why_required: The requested capability and default limit must be visible in the target.

required_outcomes.outcome: A valid batch appends every supplied item in the supplied order after existing queue contents.
required_outcomes.why_required: This defines the successful observable behavior.

required_outcomes.outcome: An empty batch is rejected before the queue changes.
required_outcomes.why_required: The request makes empty-batch rejection and no partial mutation necessary.

required_outcomes.outcome: A batch larger than the effective maximum is rejected before the queue changes.
required_outcomes.why_required: The size bound must be enforced without partially appending the batch.

required_outcomes.outcome: Existing single-item enqueue behavior remains compatible.
required_outcomes.why_required: The request explicitly protects current callers.

compatibility_constraints: Existing queue contents remain before newly appended batch items.
Existing callers of the single-item operation require no change.
acceptable_grouping: BATCH-1 and BATCH-2 may be one requirement.
BATCH-3 and BATCH-4 may be one validation requirement when both no-mutation cases remain clear.
Compatibility may be stated with successful behavior or separately.
supporting_details: A specification may name the batch operation, but the target does not require one exact method name.
A specification may discuss materializing an iterable or validating first, but those are implementation choices.
not_prescribed: Tests or documentation work as separate product requirements
